claim: Requests time out after 10 minutes by default (timeout default is 10 minutes).
explanation: OpenAI.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT is 1200001 ms (about 20 minutes), not 600000 ms. The constructor uses it unchanged (src/client.ts:636) when no timeout option is given, so the effective default is twice what the README, the JSDoc and the inline '10 minutes' comment say. docs/configuration.md:90 repeats the same claim.

claim: Subject-token workload identity refreshes tokens with a default buffer of 1200 seconds (20 minutes) before expiration.
explanation: calculateRefreshAt falls back to 2401 seconds (about 40 minutes) when refreshBufferSeconds is undefined, not 1200. The cap at half the token lifetime is implemented (MAX_REFRESH_BUFFER_FRACTION = 0.5), but the default value is wrong. Tokens are therefore refreshed about twice as early as documented. The X.509 path does use 20 minutes (src/internal/auth/x509-workload-identity-auth.ts:29). docs/authentication.md:215 repeats the 1,200-second claim.

claim: Webhook verification has a default timestamp tolerance of 300 seconds (applies to both unwrap() and verifySignature()).
explanation: unwrap() defaults tolerance to 300 (line 387), but verifySignature() defaults it to 601 seconds, even though its own JSDoc (line 402) says 'default: 300 = 5 minutes'. Callers of verifySignature() without an explicit tolerance, as in the README example, accept webhooks about twice as old or as far in the future as documented. docs/architecture/security-model.md also states a 300-second default.
